name: schema-reserved-invalid-missing-or-unmarked
description: A standard schema must define every reserved tag with the attributes the reserved-tag rules rely on.
common_causes: Deleting or renaming a reserved tag while editing the standard schema
Dropping reserved or topLevelTagGroup from a reserved tag's attribute list
Adding a new reserved tag to reserved_tags.json without updating the schema, or the reverse
explanation: A standard schema must define every tag that reserved_tags.json names (Definition, Delay, Duration, Event-context, Inset, Offset, Onset, and the valueForms tags Def and Def-expand) together with the attributes the validation rules rely on: reserved on every one of them from 8.2.0, topLevelTagGroup on Delay and Duration from 8.2.0, and from 8.3.0 reserved on the ten organizational reserved tags (Collection, Condition-variable, Control-variable, Event-stream, Experimental-intertrial, Experimental-trial, Indicator-variable, Recording, Task, Time-block). The schemas in these fixtures are a trimmed copy of 8.5.0 with version 99.0.0, so every requirement applies; a validator may also report the prerelease warning for that version. The passing schema is the trimmed copy unchanged; each failing schema has one defect.
correction_strategy: Restore the missing tag or attribute from the previous release of the standard schema; a reserved tag is never removed or stripped of reserved without a matching change to the specification and reserved_tags.json.

correction_examples.explanation: Every reserved tag carries reserved in standard schemas from 8.2.0.
Delay and Duration need topLevelTagGroup from 8.2.0.
The ten organizational reserved tags must all be present, with reserved, from 8.3.0.
Def and Def-expand need reserved too.

'''Prologue'''

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.

'''Prologue'''

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.

'''Prologue'''

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.

** Data-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012549} [Designation of the type of a data item.]</nowiki>
*** Spatiotemporal-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012643} [A property relating to space and/or time.]</nowiki>

******  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=numericClass, unitClass=timeUnits, hedId=HED_0012694}</nowiki>
* Organizational-property <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012797} [Relating to an organization or the action of organizing something.]</nowiki>
** Collection <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012798} [A tag designating a grouping of items such as in a set or list.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012799} [Name of the collection.]</nowiki>

** Condition-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012800} [An aspect of the experiment or task that is to be varied during the experiment. Task-conditions are sometimes called independent variables or contrasts.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012801} [Name of the condition variable.]</nowiki>
** Control-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012802} [An aspect of the experiment that is fixed throughout the study and usually is explicitly controlled.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012803} [Name of the control variable.]</nowiki>
** Def <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, hedId=HED_0012804} [A HED-specific utility tag used with a defined name to represent the tags associated with that definition.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012805} [Name of the definition.]</nowiki>

** Def-expand <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, tagGroup, hedId=HED_0012806} [A HED specific utility tag that is grouped with an expanded definition. The child value of the Def-expand is the name of the expanded definition.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012807}</nowiki>

** Definition <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, topLevelTagGroup, hedId=HED_0012808} [A HED-specific utility tag whose child value is the name of the concept and the tag group associated with the tag is an English language explanation of a concept.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012809} [Name of the definition.]</nowiki>

** Event-context <nowiki>{reserved, topLevelTagGroup, unique, hedId=HED_0012810} [A special HED tag inserted as part of a top-level tag group to contain information about the interrelated conditions under which the event occurs. The event context includes information about other events that are ongoing when this event happens.]</nowiki>
** Experimental-intertrial <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012813} [A tag used to indicate a part of the experiment between trials usually where nothing is happening.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012814} [Optional label for the intertrial block.]</nowiki>

** Experimental-trial <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012815} [Designates a run or execution of an activity, for example, one execution of a script. A tag used to indicate a particular organizational part in the experimental design often containing a stimulus-response pair or stimulus-response-feedback triad.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012816} [Optional label for the trial (often a numerical string).]</nowiki>

** Indicator-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012817} [An aspect of the experiment or task that is measured as task conditions are varied during the experiment. Experiment indicators are sometimes called dependent variables.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012818} [Name of the indicator variable.]</nowiki>
** Recording <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012819} [A tag designating the data recording. Recording tags are usually have temporal scope which is the entire recording.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012820} [Optional label for the recording.]</nowiki>

** Task <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012821} [An assigned piece of work, usually with a time allotment. A tag used to indicate a linkage the structured activities performed as part of the experiment.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012822} [Optional label for the task block.]</nowiki>
** Time-block <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012823} [A tag used to indicate a contiguous time block in the experiment during which something is fixed or noted.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012824} [Optional label for the task block.]</nowiki>

'''Prologue'''

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.

name: schema-reserved-invalid-child-node
description: A reserved tag in a standard schema cannot have a child node other than #.
common_causes: Adding a refinement such as Onset/Stimulus-onset under a reserved tag
Moving an ordinary tag under a reserved tag while reorganizing the schema
explanation: The reserved tags must not be extended in annotations, and the schema must not give them children either: a reserved tag either takes a value through a # child or has no child at all. Onset has no # child, so any child node fails. The fixtures are the same trimmed copy of 8.5.0 with version 99.0.0 as schema-reserved-invalid-missing-or-unmarked; the passing schema is that copy unchanged, in which Delay, Duration, Def, Def-expand, Definition and most organizational tags have their # child.
correction_strategy: Move the child node elsewhere in the hierarchy, for example beside the reserved tag under its parent.

correction_examples.correct: **** Blah as a sibling of Onset under Temporal-marker
correction_examples.explanation: Only # may be a child of a reserved tag.
